Issued at 220 PM CDT Mon Sep 14 2026

As of 19Z, the center of the stacked low pressure system is over 
northwestern ND/MT/Canadian border with the occluded/cold front 
extending southward through central SD (right along the Mo River) 
with winds west of the Mo River out of the west behind it. Temps 
range in the upper 50s and 60s with dewpoints in the 60s. So far, 
rain amounts at the office have been just below an inch for the day. 
Radar continues to show scattered showers and weak thunderstorms 
continuing east of the James River with an area of light showers or 
drizzle over portions of north central SD. Low stratus clouds 
continue (IFR/MVFR) with ceilings from 900-1500ft. As the front 
continues to track eastward, the last of the precip will exit 
eastern SD/MN by 00Z with skies clearing west to east across the 
CWA. 

Through the evening, the low continues to deepen (to ~991mb) as it 
tracks northeast into Canada with a secondary cold front/trough 
tracking northwest to southeast over the CWA on the backside of the 
low tonight through the overnight hours. As the low deepens and 
pressure gradient tightens, the northeast to southwest jet streak 
circling around the southern/backside side of the low over the 
Northern Plains increases with winds at 500mb around 60-80kts, 850mb 
winds 35-55kts, and 925mb winds 30-45kts. 6hr pressure rises by 00Z 
per GFS is about +2 to +5mb over central SD, with these values 
spreading eastward across the CWA by 06Z. We really see an increase 
in pressure rises (up to +9mb, highest central SD) 06-12Z Tuesday as 
high pressure begins to filter in. This coincides with strong CAA 
moving in, especially with secondary trough, as models indicate 850mb 
temps go from +14 to +16C at 00Z to +6 to +10 by 12Z and 925mb temps 
from +19 to +23C to +10 to +13C. So a drop in 6-9 degrees drop in 12 
hours! So pressure rises/steeper/gradients and CAA are ingredients 
for stronger winds at the surface. However, RAP soundings do indicate 
a shallow inversion developing this evening but seems to erode a bit 
with the colder/drier air moving in overnight, especially over the 
northern portions of SD. A stronger inversion does remain over south 
central and farther east you go into the CWA. This should allow for 
ongoing mixing to occur towards the surface. 

So just behind the front, surface gusts this afternoon and evening 
will be highest over central SD, particularly north central SD with 
gusts of 30 to 55 mph. There may be a brief lull/decrease in winds 
late this evening before the secondary boundary passes across the 
CWA. Therefore, the combination of the increasing winds aloft, 
stronger pressure rises, and CAA will steepen the lapse rates with 
gusts between 25-45 mph, highest over northern and northeastern SD 
through Tuesday morning. Probability of NBM wind gusts>45mph is 40-
70% over north central SD (highest Corson/Dewey to the Leola Hills) 
with a 30-50% chance along the eastern slopes of the Coteau. 24 hour 
max wind gust potential ranges from 40-60 mph, highest north central 
SD. HREF probability of gusts at or over 45 mph is upwards of 40-70% 
over north central SD and higher than NBM for Coteau ranging from 50-
75%. So blended NBM/NBM90 for winds downslope of the Coteau to 
represent this potential higher gusts. So the Wind Advisory across 
north central SD remains in effect through the overnight. If we end 
up getting more widespread wind advisory winds, then it will need to 
be expanded eastward. Also was hesitant on issuing a Wind Advisory 
for the Coteau with a lack of southwest component and the deeper 
inversion. This will also need to be monitored with the next shifts. 
As mentioned, if we develop a stronger and/or larger inversion (or 
less CAA) then the gustier winds will not mix down as effectively to 
the surface.

By Tuesday, the low/trough aloft will be northeast of the CWA with 
zonal flow as high pressure filters into the region with overall dry 
weather expected. As the high moves in, pressure gradients relax and 
the gustier winds aloft with the low move out of the area. 
Therefore, winds will decrease through Tuesday. Zonal to southwest 
flow continues Wednesday through the end of the week as a cutoff low 
aloft and its trough hovers over the western CONUS (low weakens into 
an open wave by Friday) with a ridge and mid level high 
strengthening over the central and southeastern US. Within this 
zonal to southwest flow in an active -PNA pattern, weak shortwaves 
will pass over the region Wednesday through the weekend bringing 
occasional chances of showers and thunderstorms with the best chance 
(50-80%) being late Thursday and Friday. Temperatures will overall 
be about normal ranging in upper 60s and 70s across the CWA through 
the week.
